import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.MeanValue
import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Trigonometric.Basic

set_option autoImplicit false

open Set Filter
open scoped Topology

namespace OpenGA

/-- Finite analytic data for the scalar-minimum and width argument on `[0, T]`.
This structure records inequalities and jumps only. It is not a definition of
Ricci flow, surgery, scalar curvature, or sweepout width. Supplying it from
geometric data is a separate theorem. -/
structure ScalarWidthTrace (W₀ T : ℝ) where
  count : ℕ
  count_pos : 0 < count
  times : ℕ → ℝ
  first_time : times 0 = 0
  last_time : times count = T
  times_strict : ∀ i < count, times i < times (i + 1)
  scalar : ℕ → ℝ → ℝ
  width : ℕ → ℝ → ℝ
  scalar_cont : ∀ i < count, ContinuousOn (scalar i) (Icc (times i) (times (i + 1)))
  width_cont : ∀ i < count, ContinuousOn (width i) (Icc (times i) (times (i + 1)))
  scalar_initial : -6 ≤ scalar 0 (times 0)
  width_initial : width 0 (times 0) ≤ W₀
  width_nonneg : ∀ i < count, ∀ t ∈ Icc (times i) (times (i + 1)), 0 ≤ width i t
  scalar_slope : ∀ i < count, ∀ t ∈ Ico (times i) (times (i + 1)), ∀ q : ℝ,
    q < (2 / 3 : ℝ) * (scalar i t) ^ 2 →
      ∀ᶠ s in 𝓝[>] t, q < slope (scalar i) t s
  width_slope : ∀ i < count, ∀ t ∈ Ico (times i) (times (i + 1)), ∀ q : ℝ,
    -(4 * Real.pi) - scalar i t / 2 * width i t < q →
      ∃ᶠ s in 𝓝[>] t, slope (width i) t s < q
  scalar_jump : ∀ i, i + 1 < count →
    scalar i (times (i + 1)) ≤ scalar (i + 1) (times (i + 1))
  width_jump : ∀ i, i + 1 < count →
    width (i + 1) (times (i + 1)) ≤ width i (times (i + 1))

end OpenGA

$$\forall T>0,\quad \text{there exists a scalar-width trace on }[0,T]\text{ with initial width at most }W_0.$$
A scalar-width trace is the analytic data in the imported definition: finitely many continuous scalar and nonnegative width profiles, initial scalar minimum at least $-6$, differential inequalities
$$D_+r\ge\frac23r^2,\qquad D_+w\le-4\pi-\frac12rw,$$
and upward scalar jumps and downward width jumps.

This is a composite geometric extraction target for the Kleiner-Lott surgery route with the Colding-Minicozzi width input. It deliberately isolates the unresolved passage from geometry and topology to analytic data. It is not a formalization of any one named milestone. The scope includes passing from a topological three-manifold to smooth normalized initial data, constructing surgery flows for arbitrary finite times, identifying surviving nontrivial components under the nonspherical hypothesis, and establishing the scalar/width estimates, endpoint regularity, jump inequalities, and a uniform initial width bound. None of those geometric constructions is supplied by the trace definition.

The Kleiner-Lott source starts with smooth geometric data; the topological-to-smooth passage is an additional formalization obligation in this statement.

width.explanation:
The conclusion is the explicit upper bound
$$t_n\le\left(C^{1/4}+\frac{W_0}{16\pi C^{3/4}}\right)^4-C.$$
For $\varepsilon>0$, compare every width segment with the same solution $B_\varepsilon$ of
$$B_\varepsilon'=\frac{3}{4(t+C)}B_\varepsilon-4\pi+\varepsilon,\qquad B_\varepsilon(0)=W_0+\varepsilon.$$
Its explicit expression is
$$B_\varepsilon(t)=\frac{W_0+\varepsilon}{C^{3/4}}(t+C)^{3/4}+4(\varepsilon-4\pi)\big((t+C)-C^{1/4}(t+C)^{3/4}\big).$$
At a contact point the assumed lower-Dini upper bound is strictly below the derivative of this comparison function. The one-sided comparison lemma therefore bounds the width on each interval. A downward jump preserves the endpoint inequality, so induction carries the same comparison through all intervals without changing the initial constant.

Continuity in $\varepsilon$ gives $w_{n-1}(t_n)\le B_0(t_n)$. Since the final width is nonnegative and $(t_n+C)^{3/4}>0$, factoring this expression yields
$$16\pi\big((t_n+C)^{1/4}-C^{1/4}\big)\le\frac{W_0}{C^{3/4}}.$$
Dividing by $16\pi$ and taking fourth powers proves the bound. The proof uses only Mathlib and contains no unproved geometric inputs.

root.explanation:
This is a conditional reduction of the topological Poincare conjecture to the geometric profile-extraction theorem. That child remains open. The two analytic inputs, scalar comparison and the width deadline, are proved independently.

Suppose a compact simply connected Hausdorff topological three-manifold $M$ were not homeomorphic to $S^3$. The open geometric child supplies a number $W_0$, fixed before the final time, and finite scalar-width traces on arbitrarily long intervals. The scalar comparison theorem gives
$$r_i(t)\ge-\frac6{1+4t}.$$
Because every width is nonnegative, the coupled width inequality implies
$$D_+w_i(t)\le-4\pi-\frac12r_i(t)w_i(t)\le-4\pi+\frac3{1+4t}w_i(t).$$
This is precisely the width-deadline inequality with $C=1/4$. The downward jump hypothesis permits the deadline theorem to apply across all pieces, giving
$$T\le T_*:=\left((1/4)^{1/4}+\frac{W_0}{16\pi(1/4)^{3/4}}\right)^4-\frac14.$$
Choose $T=\max(T_*,0)+1$. The geometric child supplies a trace at this positive time, while the analytic bound rules it out. This contradiction gives the required homeomorphism.

The unresolved geometric child includes smoothing, surgery existence, survival/topology, and the production of compatible scalar and width profiles. The reduction does not prove those ingredients or any of the four large geometric milestones. Every imported theorem is used in the argument; no extra import is present solely to create a graph edge.

nodes.natural_language_statement:
Let $M$ be a compact, Hausdorff, simply connected topological $3$-manifold without boundary, modelled on Euclidean $3$-space (a charted space over $\mathbb{R}^3 = $ `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)`). Then $M$ is homotopy equivalent to the standard $3$-sphere:

$$ M \simeq_h \mathbb{S}^3 = \{\, x \in \mathbb{R}^4 : \lVert x\rVert = 1 \,\}. $$

This is the classical, purely homotopy-theoretic half of the three-dimensional Poincaré conjecture; it does not use geometrization or Ricci flow. A simply connected closed $3$-manifold is orientable, so Poincaré duality forces its homology to coincide with that of $S^3$, namely $H_0 = H_3 = \mathbb{Z}$ and $H_1 = H_2 = 0$. The Hurewicz theorem then gives $\pi_3(M) \cong H_3(M) \cong \mathbb{Z}$, and a generator is represented by a map $f : S^3 \to M$ that induces isomorphisms on all homology groups. Since both $M$ and $S^3$ are simply connected CW complexes, Whitehead's theorem promotes $f$ to a homotopy equivalence.

As a milestone this is the "easy" input to the topological Poincaré conjecture: combined with the statement that every homotopy $3$-sphere is homeomorphic to $S^3$, it yields that a compact simply connected $3$-manifold is homeomorphic to $S^3$.

**Formalization Note** The sphere $\mathbb{S}^3$ is `Metric.sphere (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (3 + 1))) 1` with the subspace topology, and $\simeq_h$ is Mathlib's `ContinuousMap.HomotopyEquiv` (notation `≃ₕ`, scoped in the `ContinuousMap` namespace). No second-countability assumption is imposed, matching the parent statement `PoincareFormalization.nonempty_homeomorph_sphere_three`.

nodes.natural_language_statement:
Let $M$ be a Hausdorff topological $3$-manifold (a charted space over $\mathbb{R}^3 = $ `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)`). If $M$ is homotopy equivalent to the standard $3$-sphere, then $M$ is homeomorphic to it:

$$ \bigl(M \simeq_h \mathbb{S}^3\bigr) \;\Longrightarrow\; M \simeq_t \mathbb{S}^3 . $$

This is the deep half of the three-dimensional topological Poincaré conjecture, proved by Grigori Perelman (2002–2003) using Richard Hamilton's Ricci flow with surgery. It is precisely the $n = 3$ instance of Mathlib's `proof_wanted ContinuousMap.HomotopyEquiv.nonempty_homeomorph_sphere`, which asserts for each $n$ that a topological manifold homotopy equivalent to $\mathbb{S}^n$ is homeomorphic to it. Together with the classical fact that a closed simply connected $3$-manifold is a homotopy $3$-sphere, this statement gives the Poincaré conjecture in dimension three.

**Formalization Note** Here $\simeq_h$ is `ContinuousMap.HomotopyEquiv` (notation `≃ₕ`) and $\simeq_t$ is `Homeomorph` (notation `≃ₜ`); the sphere is `Metric.sphere (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (3 + 1))) 1`. The hypothesis is a bare homotopy equivalence, matching the shape of the sibling `proof_wanted`; no compactness or simple-connectivity hypothesis is required beyond the homotopy equivalence itself.

nodes.theorem_title: Scalar and width traces across surgery times
nodes.natural_language_statement:
For real numbers $W_0,T$, a scalar-width trace consists of a positive finite number of intervals with
$$0=t_0<t_1<\cdots<t_n=T,$$
and continuous real functions $r_i,w_i$ on each $[t_i,t_{i+1}]$. The initial bounds are $r_0(0)\ge-6$ and $w_0(0)\le W_0$, and all widths are nonnegative. On each right-open interval the lower right Dini derivatives obey
$$D_+r_i\ge\frac23 r_i^2,\qquad D_+w_i\le-4\pi-\frac12r_iw_i.$$
At each internal joining time, the scalar profile can jump upward and the width can jump downward:
$$r_i(t_{i+1})\le r_{i+1}(t_{i+1}),\qquad w_{i+1}(t_{i+1})\le w_i(t_{i+1}).$$
Here $D_+$ denotes the liminf of forward difference quotients. Scalar lower bounds are expressed by eventual strict slope bounds; width upper bounds use frequent strict slope bounds. A limsup upper bound, as in the geometric width estimate, implies the latter hypothesis.

This is an analytic interface assembled from the scalar comparison and width estimates. It does not define Ricci flow, surgery, scalar curvature, or geometric sweepout width. Producing these data from a manifold remains a separate geometric theorem.

import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.MeanValue
import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Trigonometric.Basic

set_option autoImplicit false

open Set Filter
open scoped Topology

namespace OpenGA

/-- Finite analytic data for the scalar-minimum and width argument on `[0, T]`.
This structure records inequalities and jumps only. It is not a definition of
Ricci flow, surgery, scalar curvature, or sweepout width. Supplying it from
geometric data is a separate theorem. -/
structure ScalarWidthTrace (W₀ T : ℝ) where
  count : ℕ
  count_pos : 0 < count
  times : ℕ → ℝ
  first_time : times 0 = 0
  last_time : times count = T
  times_strict : ∀ i < count, times i < times (i + 1)
  scalar : ℕ → ℝ → ℝ
  width : ℕ → ℝ → ℝ
  scalar_cont : ∀ i < count, ContinuousOn (scalar i) (Icc (times i) (times (i + 1)))
  width_cont : ∀ i < count, ContinuousOn (width i) (Icc (times i) (times (i + 1)))
  scalar_initial : -6 ≤ scalar 0 (times 0)
  width_initial : width 0 (times 0) ≤ W₀
  width_nonneg : ∀ i < count, ∀ t ∈ Icc (times i) (times (i + 1)), 0 ≤ width i t
  scalar_slope : ∀ i < count, ∀ t ∈ Ico (times i) (times (i + 1)), ∀ q : ℝ,
    q < (2 / 3 : ℝ) * (scalar i t) ^ 2 →
      ∀ᶠ s in 𝓝[>] t, q < slope (scalar i) t s
  width_slope : ∀ i < count, ∀ t ∈ Ico (times i) (times (i + 1)), ∀ q : ℝ,
    -(4 * Real.pi) - scalar i t / 2 * width i t < q →
      ∃ᶠ s in 𝓝[>] t, slope (width i) t s < q
  scalar_jump : ∀ i, i + 1 < count →
    scalar i (times (i + 1)) ≤ scalar (i + 1) (times (i + 1))
  width_jump : ∀ i, i + 1 < count →
    width (i + 1) (times (i + 1)) ≤ width i (times (i + 1))

end OpenGA

nodes.natural_language_statement:
Let $M$ be a compact simply connected Hausdorff topological three-manifold without boundary. Suppose that $M$ is not homeomorphic to the unit three-sphere. Then there is a real number $W_0\ge0$, independent of the final time, such that
$$\forall T>0,\quad \text{there exists a scalar-width trace on }[0,T]\text{ with initial width at most }W_0.$$
A scalar-width trace is the analytic data in the imported definition: finitely many continuous scalar and nonnegative width profiles, initial scalar minimum at least $-6$, differential inequalities
$$D_+r\ge\frac23r^2,\qquad D_+w\le-4\pi-\frac12rw,$$
and upward scalar jumps and downward width jumps.

This is a composite geometric extraction target for the Kleiner-Lott surgery route with the Colding-Minicozzi width input. It deliberately isolates the unresolved passage from geometry and topology to analytic data. It is not a formalization of any one named milestone. The scope includes passing from a topological three-manifold to smooth normalized initial data, constructing surgery flows for arbitrary finite times, identifying surviving nontrivial components under the nonspherical hypothesis, and establishing the scalar/width estimates, endpoint regularity, jump inequalities, and a uniform initial width bound. None of those geometric constructions is supplied by the trace definition.

The Kleiner-Lott source starts with smooth geometric data; the topological-to-smooth passage is an additional formalization obligation in this statement.

nodes.explanation:
We prove the three-dimensional topological Poincaré conjecture in the form
$$ \text{$M$ compact, Hausdorff, simply connected, a topological $3$-manifold} \

This is a conditional reduction of the topological Poincare conjecture to the geometric profile-extraction theorem. That child remains open. The two analytic inputs, scalar comparison and the width deadline, are proved independently.

Suppose a compact simply connected Hausdorff topological three-manifold $M$ were not homeomorphic to $S^3$. The open geometric child supplies a number $W_0$, fixed before the final time, and finite scalar-width traces on arbitrarily long intervals. The scalar comparison theorem gives
$$r_i(t)\ge-\frac6{1+4t}.$$
Because every width is nonnegative, the coupled width inequality implies
$$D_+w_i(t)\le-4\pi-\frac12r_i(t)w_i(t)\le-4\pi+\frac3{1+4t}w_i(t).$$
This is precisely the width-deadline inequality with $C=1/4$. The downward jump hypothesis permits the deadline theorem to apply across all pieces, giving
$$T\le T_*:=\left((1/4)^{1/4}+\frac{W_0}{16\pi(1/4)^{3/4}}\right)^4-\frac14.$$
Choose $T=\max(T_*,0)+1$. The geometric child supplies a trace at this positive time, while the analytic bound rules it out. This contradiction gives the required homeomorphism.

The unresolved geometric child includes smoothing, surgery existence, survival/topology, and the production of compatible scalar and width profiles. The reduction does not prove those ingredients or any of the four large geometric milestones. Every imported theorem is used in the argument; no extra import is present solely to create a graph edge.
